panic.format: pthread kernel extension not loaded (function table is NULL). @%s:%d
panic.reading: bsd_init calls pthread_init(); it panics unless the pthread kext has called pthread_kext_register() to fill _pthread_functions
panic.format_captured_automatically: The fixture now reads the panic format string from x0 itself and records it as panic_format, so a run explains its own panic without a separate --read-at.

finding: A multiprocessor emulated machine gets past the GIC target probe: gicv2::Controller::prepareLocal is reached (it was not with --smp 1), the kernel enters bsd_init -- a milestone this port had never reached -- and then panics with 'pthread kernel extension not loaded (function table is NULL)'. The linked image does contain _pthread_functions, _pthread_kext_register and the pthread kext symbols, so the gap is that the kext never starts and registers, not that it is missing from the link.
corrected_earlier_reading: QEMU's hw/intc/arm_gic.c returns 0 for the whole target register range only when num_cpu == 1 ('For uniprocessor GICs these RAZ/WI'); with two or more CPUs it reports cm for the banked SGI/PPI range. The handset GIC is multiprocessor, so the ArmCpu probe is probably correct on hardware: the earlier note that it 'may be wrong on the handset too' was wrong.
not_proven: XNU entry or iOS userland on a handset
that the pthread kext can be started on this port (its dependencies are unexamined)
anything about the eMMC, display or GPU on real hardware

prelink_closure._note: from out/lumia950/kernel/kernel.json in the kernel artifact of run 44003233713
prelink_closure.reading: board.toml [kernel.prelink] roots names four kernelcache components; the prelink adds what those declare as libraries. The pthread kext is not a library of any of them, so it is not in the closure, its start routine never runs, pthread_kext_register() is never called, and _pthread_functions stays NULL.

next_action: Add the pthread kext to [kernel.prelink] roots. Its kernelcache component name is unknown here and must be read from the iOS 16.7.16 kernelcache's component list, not guessed: the kernel build runs on CI macOS, which currently does not start. The image already contains _pthread_kext_register and _pthread_functions (the xnu shims), so nothing else is missing from the link.
